<reason>A won by keeping the motion on slowing development, not currently fielded weapons, and by converting B’s own “national emergency” language into evidence that the delay is real. B’s case on leaky controls and taxing allied learning was serious, but it never resolved treating lost compute as a rounding error for the adversary and a durable hit at home. A’s weighing—compounding training friction against relocated revenue—was the cleaner vote path.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s turn of B’s workarounds into conceded delay, then the later trap: a mere “budget line” cannot also be a “national emergency,” which B’s “industrial not military” reply never fully dissolved.</best_rebuttal>
